'''Yuga Shrine''' (瑜伽神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Takabatakechō]], [[Nara (city)|Nara]], [[Nara Prefecture]], on Yuga Mountain.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the sacred mountain [[Asuka Kannabi]] was relocated to this site with the establishment of [[Heijō-kyō]], and the mountain was subsequently called the Asuka Mountain of Heijō{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}. Initially, the shrine served as the guardian of [[Gangō-ji|Gango-ji]] [[Q104539457]], protecting against misfortune from the [[Kimon]] direction. Later, when [[Daijō-in]] of [[Kōfuku-ji]] was built at the foot of the mountain, the shrine was venerated by the [[Fujiwara clan]] and others{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}.

The ''[[Daijōin Jisha Zōjiki]]'' records an entry from December 30, 1494, stating "Ichigo Chieko-in-den Go-kenchiku no Bun ... Imamiyaden Goten Dō Haiden Kari-fuki ya," identifying "Imamiya" as referring to this shrine. It is said that "Imamiya" was used in contrast to the original shrine in Asuka{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}. The current name, Yuga Shrine, has been in use only relatively recently{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=81}}.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Yuga Mountain Cherry and Maple Monument ===
<blockquote>
In spring, the flowers bloom again upon Yuga Mountain.
Today’s autumn leaves, one hesitates to part from.
</blockquote>
The poem was composed by [[Yoshiki Kajino]], also known as Kajino Tosa-no-kami Fujiwara no Yoshitaka. He served as the [[Ongoku-bugyō]] from April 8, 1831, until his transfer as the Kyoto West Magistrate on December 8, 1837. He also authored ''[[Yamashiro Yamato Kenbun Zuihitsu]]'' ("An Essay on Observations in Yamashiro and Yamato").

Yuga Mountain has been famous for its cherry blossoms and autumn foliage since ancient times and is included among the [[Sixteen Views of Nara]], featuring "Yuga Mountain Cherry Blossoms" and "Yuga Mountain Autumn Leaves"{{sfn|Nara City History: Shrines and Temples|p=80}}.

=== "Asuka of Heijō" Manyō Poem Monument ===
<blockquote>
The Asuka of my old home is now in ruin,
Yet fair is Asuka of Nara,
How beautiful it remains.
</blockquote>
This poem was composed by [[Ōtomo no Sakanoue no Iratsume]] in the fifth year of [[Tenpyō]], corresponding to 733 CE.

== Access ==
* By train: The shrine is accessible from [[Kintetsu Nara Station]], followed by a short walk.
* By car: Parking is available near the shrine grounds.
